reason: The final full correctness audit over 1dd01581..9feeae6 produced nine deduplicated candidates. Independent adjudication confirmed four lifecycle defects: initial publication can race stale reclaim, stale claimant deletion is not generation-safe, partial slice startup has two cleanup owners, and an earlier body error can suppress a teardown signal. Those confirmed fixes must pass validation and another frozen-range audit before this boundary is clean.

boundary.startingEvent: A random level arrival selects its destination before committing coordinates, a three-line status row composes hunger and capacity fields, ordinary movement admits or rejects a destination, or a mutation command reclaims or tears down its aggregate slice.
boundary.endingEvent: Arrival pickup and floor description either complete through the next prompt or refuse before any observable change; the status row contains both fields; movement exposes its public boundary error; or the mutation command exits or re-raises its signal with live ownership preserved whenever cleanup is incomplete.
boundary.validInputs: Random arrivals while helpless, with autopickup disabled, with ordinary and shop-owned floor objects, and with supported ordinary pickup; satiated plus strained three-line status; unsupported destination object naming; concurrent stale-lock reclaim, partial slice startup, cleanup failure, SIGINT, and SIGTERM.
boundary.observables: Hero and room state, inventory and floor ownership, achievement/billing/keeper state, messages, complete screens and cursors, PRNG log, public error class, process result or signal, lock owner record, cgroup ownership, descendant cleanup, and subsequent invocation availability.
boundary.exclusions: Unported shop billing/debit settlement remains fail-closed before movement; the full shop-edge blocking dialogue remains deferred behind an atomic admission stop; unsupported arrival pickup and naming branches stop before the planned destination is committed; no sealed holdout evidence is used. Other prior generated-shop price exclusions remain unchanged.

candidateListMethod.upstreamEntryPoints: Traced hack.c domove_core through pickup.c check_here and invent.c look_here's single-object and pile doname_with_price call sites, then objnam.c doname_base(DONAME_WITH_PRICE) and shk.c get_cost_of_shop_item, get_pricing_units, get_cost, getprice, oid_price_adjustment, and record_price_quote.
candidateListMethod.dispatchTablesAndCatalogs: Cross-checked object classes and oc_cost data, generated SHTYPES rooms and keepers, quantity and Charisma partitions, quote sentinels, inventory currency wording, room-number buffers, and pile_limit's count-versus-menu split.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: Followed get_obj_location, in_rooms, inside_shop, shop_keeper, inhishop, ordinary naming, price rounding, currency, and the object-chain loop. contained_cost and billing are excluded because valid objects are top-level non-containers.
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: Inspected js/hack.js costly_spot refusal, js/invent.js look_here preflight and both naming sites, js/objnam.js preflight/discovery ownership, js/shk.js generated-shop queries and quote helpers, js/light.js object location, js/rooms.js current-shop state, and existing shop/object-pile tests and fresh runners.
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: The fresh case validates a natural single generated-shop stock object because stock_room creates one object per square; a direct movement integration must separately prove the reviewed two-member menu and its atomic excluded-second-member refusal.

entries.reachability: The unmarked CLI has launched a long mutation run and receives SIGINT or SIGTERM, or a concurrent invocation is refused while another run owns the exclusivity lock.
entries.owner: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs outer launcher and exclusivity owner
entries.effects: Forward cancellation only to the owned run, await cleanup, reproduce the caller-visible signal, and prevent a refused contender from stopping the owner.
entries.evidence: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs now acquires an owner-record lock, launches systemd-run asynchronously, forwards SIGINT and SIGTERM through its uniquely named aggregate slice, awaits cleanup, and re-raises the signal. The real-process regression refuses a contender while the owner remains live, cancels the owner with SIGTERM, confirms the slice is inactive, then proves the next invocation can acquire the lock. A stale-lock regression stops the dead owner's recorded slice before replacement.

entries.reachability: The outer mutator owns an active per-wave scope under memory/task limits and is cancelled or resource-limited.
entries.owner: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs systemd unit topology
entries.effects: Place outer and wave scopes beneath one uniquely owned aggregate slice so limits and cancellation contain the full process tree.
entries.evidence: Each invocation creates one underscore-named aggregate slice with the 2 GiB, zero-swap and 64-task limits. mutationCgroupArgs and testRunnerCommand place the outer scope and every production wave beneath it. The live outer regression reads both ControlGroup values and proves the scope is a descendant of the slice; command-shape tests pin the same ancestry for waves.

entries.effects: Preserve the runner result while collecting every helper and the uniquely owned wave scope after ordinary completion.
entries.evidence: runTests now stops its uniquely named wave scope after every result and accepts a result only after systemd confirms the cgroup is empty. The ordinary-completion fixture spawns its helper with detached:true, proves the runner result remains passing, and proves the helper pid no longer exists.

entries.reachability: Two reclaimers observe a stale owner while one replacement owner can acquire the main lock between their reads.
entries.owner: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs stale-reclaim claim inode and incumbent revalidation

entries.evidence: scripts/mutate-sites.test.mjs deterministically interleaves two reclaimers with a replacement owner and proves the replacement lock and slice survive.

entries.reachability: Aggregate startup partially succeeds, or stop/reset verification fails during ordinary completion or cancellation.
entries.owner: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs sliceNeedsCleanup state and owner-lock release
entries.effects: Retain the sole recovery owner record until aggregate cleanup is proven, so the next stale acquisition stops the recorded slice before replacement.
entries.evidence: scripts/mutate-sites.test.mjs injects both post-start cleanup failure and partial-start failure, then proves the next invocation recovers the recorded unit.

entries.candidate: OS signal preservation through synchronous teardown
entries.reachability: SIGINT or SIGTERM arrives while mutation cleanup occupies the synchronous teardown interval.
entries.owner: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs queued signal settling and re-raise path
entries.effects: Give queued signal handlers one event-loop turn before removal, complete owned cleanup, and terminate with the original OS signal.
entries.evidence: scripts/mutate-sites.test.mjs sends real SIGINT and SIGTERM during synchronous teardown and verifies both aggregate cleanup and caller-visible signal termination.

entries.candidate: Serialized initial lock publication and stale reclaim
entries.reachability: An initializer pauses after creating or writing its pending lock while a contender judges the owner absent or stale after the grace interval.
entries.owner: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs mutation publication/reclaim claim
entries.effects: Use the same exclusive claim for initial owner publication and stale replacement so a live owner cannot appear between a reclaimer's final read and directory removal.
entries.evidence: acquireMutationLock now acquires the complete-inode claim before mkdir, pending-owner rename, live-owner validation, stale-slice cleanup, and replacement. Publication hooks prove a contender is refused while the original complete owner record survives.

entries.reachability: A crashed reclaimer leaves a dead claim and two later contenders can overlap their claimant read and unlink operations.
entries.owner: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs acquireMutationLockClaim
entries.effects: Never unlink the shared claim based on a prior liveness read; fail closed with the preserved dead owner identity rather than risk deleting a replacement claimant.
entries.evidence: The dead-claim regression proves acquisition refuses, preserves the exact claimant record, and creates no main lock. The serialized replacement regression proves one held claim refuses a second publisher.

entries.reachability: The slice starts but setting runtime limits fails.
entries.owner: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs runInMutationCgroup outer lifecycle
entries.effects: Leave all partial-start cleanup to the outer owner, which stops once and releases the lock only after cleanup succeeds.
entries.evidence: startMutationSlice no longer stops internally. The partial-start regression pins start/set-property without an inner stop, then proves the outer sequence is acquire, start, one stop, release while retaining the original startup error.

entries.candidate: Teardown signal precedence over prior body failure
entries.reachability: The mutation child or protected body fails, then SIGINT or SIGTERM arrives during synchronous aggregate teardown.
entries.owner: scripts/mutate-sites.mjs runInMutationCgroup terminal outcome
entries.effects: Store body and cleanup errors until handlers settle, then re-raise a recorded caller signal before propagating stored errors.
entries.evidence: Injected schedules cover both signals after child error, and real subprocess schedules cover both normal and failed children receiving both OS signals during synchronous teardown; all clean ownership and terminate with the original signal.

entries.reachability: A maintainer reads the changed status shrink order, look_here boundary, doname pricing ownership, quote lifecycle, or getprice preconditions.
entries.owner: js/display.js, js/invent.js, js/objnam.js, and js/shk.js comments/private API
entries.effects: Make the exact phase order, fail-closed branches, pricing owner, quote writer/consumer lifecycle, and production preconditions explicit.
entries.evidence: The status comment now names the capacity-abbreviation phase; look_here names its visible-region and seen-trap fail-closed boundary; shk.js describes the live quote writer, future remembered-price consumer, and get_cost_of_shop_item precondition owner. donameFresh no longer exposes a withPrice option: only private donameFreshInternal can admit the live price suffix, and the public bypass regression test was observed red before the fix. Worktree mutation killed all four changed objnam mutants, including both sides of that private delegation.

sourceReview: The repeated source review traces the random-arrival transaction through do.c goto_level/u_on_rndspot/u_on_newpos, pickup.c check_here/pickup, invent.c look_here, display.c status composition, movement admission ownership, and the mutation runner's lock/slice/signal lifecycle. The final audit added exact publication-versus-reclaim and claimant-read-versus-unlink schedules, partial set-property startup, and child-error-plus-teardown-signal order. It rejected five candidates with concrete production reachability or explicit-boundary evidence and confirmed the four lifecycle defects now assigned above. No known gameplay gap remains inside the boundary; lifecycle readiness awaits broad validation and a repeated full audit.
